key_insight: A compact set of consistent DNA methylation features can classify CNS tumors accurately across platforms while remaining interpretable for diagnostics.
clinical_relevance: This approach could make routine neuro-oncology testing more scalable, help resolve difficult tumor cases, and support diagnostics on both array and sequencing workflows.
method: Selected informative CpG regions using variance filtering, consistency checks, and elastic-net logistic regression
Trained a linear SVM on methylation array data and adapted it to sequencing data with imputation
Used low-dimensional feature sets to distinguish tumor classes, including highly similar entities
evidence_signal: In external array-based validation cohorts (n=1,993), the classifier reached 0.96 accuracy and retained robust performance on bisulfite-equivalent targeted sequencing and Nanopore data.
watch_item: Cross-platform deployment may still depend on careful handling of missing data, assay-specific preprocessing, and prospective validation in routine clinical settings.
paper_title: Consistent DNA methylation patterns enable accurate and interpretable cross-platform classification of central nervous system tumors
